summary: Backend production-hardening tests (v3) executed. 32/32 pytest tests PASS covering: health, auth (unauth 401s, dev-login, /me, refresh rotation, logout revocation), cross-user data isolation (tasks/events/sources/export/courses across two dev-login users), security (public /wipe removed, DELETE /me deletes+revokes sessions, oversized import 413, /auth/dev-login rate-limits to 429), AI-degradation to clean 503 (capture, import, notes/generate, transcribe) and non-AI CRUD (tasks incl. patch to done, events, briefing structure, courses+detail, timeline filters, evening-review, weekly-review, prefs GET/PUT). AI is NOT configured (OPENAI_API_KEY empty) — behavior matches spec.

minor.issue: Return 200 {ok:true} even when the resource does not exist or belongs to another user. No security leak (user_id filter enforced) but clients cannot distinguish success from silent no-op. Consider returning 404 when matched_count == 0.

When no user chunks match the query, returns 200 with a hard-coded fallback message without invoking AI. This is fine, but as a side-effect the AI-503 path for /search is only reachable after data has been ingested via /capture, /import, /notes or /transcribe — none of which work without OPENAI_API_KEY. Effectively /search cannot be exercised end-to-end in this env.

Uses per-process defaultdict keyed by request.client.host. Behind multi-pod ingress each pod has its own counter, so effective limit ≈ N×limit. Works for basic abuse control but noted for prod scaling — move to Redis-backed limiter.

action_items: Optional: return 404 from DELETE /tasks/{tid} and /events/{eid} when matched_count == 0 for clearer client semantics.
Optional: swap in-memory rate limiter for a Redis/shared store implementation before production scale-out.
To fully exercise AI endpoints, set OPENAI_API_KEY in /app/backend/.env — expected behavior in current run is 503, which is correct.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~765 lines and mixes helpers, auth routes, CRUD and AI orchestration. Consider splitting into routers (auth.py routes, tasks_router.py, events_router.py, ai_router.py, briefing.py) for maintainability (>700 line threshold).

Global AsyncOpenAI _client is cached in ai_service.py; when OPENAI_API_KEY is later set at runtime, the cached None-path still raises AIError first request — that's fine since key is env-var only at startup. Just note documentation.

config.validate() logs a warning at import but does not fail startup. Acceptable for dev, but for prod hardening consider raising in server.py startup when JWT_SECRET is a dev placeholder AND ALLOW_INSECURE_DEV=false.
JWT_SECRET currently reads 'dev-only-change-me-...' — validate() accepts it because it's >=16 chars. Add a check to reject known-placeholder strings for production.
seed_data_creation: Test-created users are prefixed TEST_user_a_/TEST_user_b_/TEST_refresh_/TEST_logout_/TEST_delete_/TEST_rl_. Test tasks/events are TEST_-prefixed. DELETE /me tests self-clean their data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use POST /api/auth/dev-login with any email to get JWTs (ALLOW_INSECURE_DEV=true). BASE URL: https://semester-sync-7.preview.emergentagent.com. All AI endpoints return 503 by design (OPENAI_API_KEY empty). Rate-limit test resets require ~60s between runs; the test itself fires 120 requests with Connection:close to trip at least one pod. Full suite runs in ~17s from a cold-window state.
rca_of_issue: No open issues. Initial rate-limit test flake was caused by requests.Session keep-alive + multi-pod ingress each keeping its own in-memory counter (~40/pod/min). Resolved by firing enough non-persistent requests (120) to saturate any single pod's window.
